review: The hymn is a pilgrim song of ascent: 1:2 is Ps 121:1 (אֶשָּׂא עֵינַי אֶל־הֶהָרִים) with Ps 25:4, 2:4 Ps 24:7 (שְׁעָרִים … הִנָּשְׂאוּ), 2:5–6 1 Pet 2:21 (לְמַעַן תֵּלְכוּ בַּעֲקֵבוֹתָיו), and 3:3–4 Ps 51:12–13 with Ps 139:23–24.

1:1 is a single word, matching the printed يَا يَسُوعُ of the first stanza, which is why the 4/8/8 shape begins with a one-word line; it is not padded to a full line, since the invocation is the tune's pickup and not a stanza line.

2:6 אֵלֵךְ בְּעִקְבוֹתֶיךָ — the Arabic سَوْفَ أَتْبَعُ خُطَاك is 'I will follow Your footsteps'; עִקְבוֹת is the heel-track word of Ps 89:52 and Song 1:8, and the same noun recurs in 2:5 as a verb, so walking and following are one act in the stanza.

3:4 מְטַהֵר לְבָבוֹת — the Arabic يَا مُطَهِّرَ الْقُلُوب is a vocative title; the Hebrew keeps the participle as a title with הוֹי, since a construct 'Purifier of hearts' would need a noun Hebrew does not have for the office.

3:7–8 חָפַצְתִּי לִשְׁכֹּן אִתְּךָ — the Arabic قَدْ رَغِبْتُ فِي الْبَقَاءِ مَعكَ is 'I longed to remain with You'; the Hebrew keeps the infinitive of שָׁכַן (Ps 15:1, מִי־יִשְׁכֹּן בְּהַר־קָדְשֶׁךָ) so the last line answers the psalm's question rather than expressing a general wish.
